what_its_for: This medicine is applied to your skin to help relieve minor aches and pains in your muscles and joints. It may be used for back pain, arthritis, sprains, strains, and bruises. It works by creating a warming and cooling feeling on your skin that helps distract your brain from deeper pain.
how_to_take: Apply a thin layer of this medicine directly to the painful area of your skin. Gently rub it in until it is absorbed. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water right after applying, unless you are treating your hands. Do NOT apply to broken, irritated, or sunburned skin. Do NOT cover the treated area tightly with a bandage or wrap after applying, as this can cause burns. Do NOT use near your eyes, mouth, or private areas. Do NOT apply before or after activities that cause heavy sweating (like exercising or bathing in hot water), as this can increase the risk of serious skin irritation or burns.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: Apply to the affected area up to 3 to 4 times per day, or as directed on the package label. Do not use more than directed. Each product may have slightly different instructions, so always read the label of the specific product you are using. Do NOT use on children under 12 years old without first talking to a doctor.
missed_dose: This medicine is used as needed for pain relief, so there is no regular dosing schedule to follow. If you forget to apply it, simply use it when you remember or when you feel pain again. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the cap or lid tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on your genitals — if this happens, rinse with plenty of cool water right away. Avoid applying heat (like a heating pad, hot water bottle, or heat lamp) to the treated area, as this can cause serious burns. Avoid tight bandages or wraps over treated skin. Avoid touching your face or eyes after application until your hands are thoroughly washed. Avoid using near an open flame. Do not use this medicine at the same time as other topical pain products on the same area of skin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical attention right away if you experience: severe burning, blistering, redness, or swelling at the application site; signs of a serious skin reaction; pain that spreads or gets worse; numbness in the treated area; accidental ingestion of this product (call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 immediately); or if your pain does not improve after 7 days of use, or if it goes away and comes back within a few days. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any allergies to peppers (capsaicin comes from chili peppers).
when_it_works: You may feel a warming, tingling, or cooling sensation within minutes of applying this medicine. Pain relief usually begins within 15 to 30 minutes. For best results with regular use, it may take several days of consistent application for maximum benefit, especially for arthritis or chronic pain. If you do not notice any improvement after 7 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, especially in the first trimester or near your due date. Children: Do not use in children under 12 years old without a doctor's advice. Older Adults: Use with caution, as older adults may have more sensitive skin and a higher risk of skin irritation or burns. People with Allergies to Peppers: Avoid this product if you are allergic to hot peppers or pepper-based products, as capsaicin is derived from chili peppers. People with Sensitive Skin or Skin Conditions: Talk to your doctor before use if you have eczema, psoriasis, or other skin conditions.
